title: Locally Balancing Signed Graphs

problem.claim: The paper addresses modifying signed graphs to maximize the number of vertices whose participating triangles are positive.

gap.claim: Existing research primarily emphasizes global balance and lengthy cycles representing distant interactions rather than local balance.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces the Locally Balancing Signed Graph problem, which aims to maximize locally balanced vertices through graph modification.
The paper proposes a greedy method for the NP-hard LBS problem despite the absence of monotonicity and submodularity.
The method is enhanced with dynamic computation and pruning techniques.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their greedy method as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show the efficacy of their greedy method for solving the LBS problem.
The authors report substantial runtime reductions from their optimization techniques.

narrative_sequence.summary: Signed graphs model positive and negative relationships, and balance is presented as a fundamental concept.
Unbalanced vertices are associated with cognitive dissonance and emotional disturbance, motivating graph modification.
Prior work is characterized as focusing mainly on global balance and lengthy cycles.
The paper defines local balance using positive participating triangles, formulates the LBS problem, and proposes a greedy method with dynamic computation and pruning.
The authors report experimental efficacy and substantial runtime reductions.

source_observation.claim: The paper distinguishes local balance based on positive triangles from global balance based on lengthy cycles.

interpretation.claim: Choosing a locality level can align a graph objective more closely with immediate relationships.

application.claim: For relationship-analysis tasks, consider objectives based on short cycles when immediate interactions are the intended focus.

exception.claim: This lesson may not apply when distant interactions and global balance are the primary analytical target.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the graph-modification operations.
The abstract does not provide datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or quantitative runtime results.
The abstract does not describe the greedy algorithm or the dynamic computation and pruning techniques in detail.
